chapterNote: Wisdom before thrones, and wisdom before the grave. The chapter opens with court counsel: keep the king's command for the sake of your oath before God, do not bolt from his presence or dig in behind a bad cause, for his word is backed by power and no one calls him to account. But the wise heart knows what the king does not — that every matter has its own time and judgment coming — and the chapter walks steadily toward the throne no king escapes: no man has authority over the day of death, there is no discharge in that war. From verse 10 the Preacher stares down the scandal of delayed justice: the wicked get honored burials, sentence is not executed speedily and hearts fill up with evil because of it, and sometimes the righteous receive the wicked man's wages and the wicked the righteous man's. His confession holds both wires at once — I know it will be well with those who fear God, and I see the days when it looks otherwise. So he commends joy again, and closes with the deepest bow in the book: even the wise man who claims to know cannot find out the work of God.

1.text: Who is like the wise man, and who else knows the interpretation of a matter? A man's wisdom lights up his face, and the hardness of his features is transformed.
1.amp: Who is as the wise [chakam] man? and who knows [yada] the interpretation [pesher] of a thing [dabar]? a man's [adam] wisdom [chokmah] makes his face [panim] to shine [or], and the boldness ['the strength', oz, the KJV margin] of his face shall be changed.
1.notes: pesher (H6592), interpretation, is the word Daniel's court-tales use for unlocking dreams (cf. Daniel 2). chokmah does to the panim (H6440) what it does to the man: or (H215), it shines — and the oz (H5797), the hard set of the jaw, softens into light.

2.text: I counsel you: keep the king's command, and do it for the sake of your oath before God.
2.amp: I counsel you to keep [shamar] the king's [melek] commandment [peh — his mouth, his word], and that in regard [dibrah] of the oath [shebuah] of God [Elohim].
2.notes: The king's 'commandment' is literally his peh (H6310), his mouth. The ground of obedience is not the king's worth but the shebuah (H7621), the sworn allegiance taken before Elohim: loyalty to the crown as a duty owed higher up (cf. Romans 13:1).

3.text: Do not be quick to walk out of his presence, and do not take your stand in an evil cause, for he does whatever he pleases.
3.amp: Be not hasty [bahal] to go [yalak] out of his sight [panim — his presence]: stand [amad] not in an evil [ra] thing [dabar]; for he does [asah] whatsoever pleases [chaphets] him.
3.notes: Two court-errors: bolting from the panim (H6440) in visible protest, and amad (H5975), planting one's feet, behind a bad cause. Both forget the arithmetic of thrones — the king's chaphets (H2654), his pleasure, is enforceable and yours is not.

4.text: For where the word of a king is, there is power, and who can say to him, 'What are you doing?'
4.amp: Where the word [dabar] of a king [melek] is, there is power [shilton — authority]: and who may say [amar] unto him, 'What are you doing [asah]?'
4.notes: The unanswerable question — 'What doest thou?' — is elsewhere asked of God alone (cf. Job 9:12; Daniel 4:35). The king's dabar carries shilton (H7983), executive power; the parallel quietly reminds us whose word carries more.

5.text: Whoever keeps the commandment will meet no evil thing, and a wise heart knows both the right time and the right judgment.
5.amp: Whoso keeps [shamar] the commandment [mitsvah] shall feel ['shall know', yada, the KJV margin] no evil [ra] thing [dabar]: and a wise man's [chakam] heart [leb] discerns [yada] both time [et] and judgment [mishpat].
5.notes: mitsvah (H4687), the command: obedience is the near-term shield. But the chakam's leb (H3820) carries a compass the courtier needs — yada (H3045) of the et (H6256) and the mishpat (H4941), the sense of when to act and what verdict is coming.

6.text: For every matter has its own time and its own judgment, even while man's misery lies heavy upon him.
6.amp: Because to every purpose [chephets] there is [yesh] time [et] and judgment [mishpat], therefore the misery [ra] of man [adam] is great [rav] upon him.
6.notes: The poem of chapter 3 restated with a courtroom edge: every chephets (H2656) has an appointed et and a mishpat waiting. The weight (rav, H7227) man lives under is partly this — the verdict is certain and the docket is sealed.

7.text: For he does not know what is coming; who can tell him how and when it will be?
7.amp: For he knows [yada] not that which shall be: for who can tell [nagad — declare] him when ['how', the KJV margin] it shall be?
7.notes: nagad (H5046), to declare: no herald runs ahead of tomorrow. The blindfold of 6:12 is permanent equipment under the sun, for kings and courtiers alike.

8.text: No man has authority over the spirit, to hold the breath back, and no man has authority over the day of death. There is no discharge in that war, and wickedness will not rescue those who are given to it.
8.amp: There is no man [adam] that has power over the spirit [ruach] to retain [kala — restrain, hold in] the spirit; neither has he power in the day [yom] of death [mavet]: and there is no discharge ['casting off weapons', the KJV margin] in that war [milchamah]; neither shall wickedness [resha] deliver [malat] those that are given [baal — the masters, the practicers] to it.
8.notes: kala (H3607) is to shut in or restrain: the ruach (H7307), the breath-spirit, cannot be held one hour past its release. The milchamah (H4421) against death grants no furlough, and resha (H7562) — the crooked man's favorite escape hatch — will not malat (H4422), deliver, its own baal (H1167), its master.

9.text: All this I saw as I gave my heart to every work that is done under the sun: there is a time when one man rules over another to that man's hurt.
9.amp: All this have I seen [raah], and applied [natan] my heart [leb] unto every work [maaseh] that is done [asah] under the sun [shemesh]: there is a time [et] wherein one man [adam] rules over another to his own hurt [ra].
9.notes: Power under the sun runs person-to-person and often wound-first: the ruling-word (H7980, shalat) with ra (H7451) attached. The Hebrew leaves open whose hurt — the ruled man's or, in the end, the ruler's own; history supplies examples of both.

10.text: Then too I saw the wicked buried with honor, men who used to come and go from the holy place, and they were soon forgotten in the very city where they had done so. This also is vapor.
10.amp: And so I saw [raah] the wicked [rasha] buried [qabar], who had come [bo] and gone [halak] from the place [maqom] of the holy [qadosh], and they were forgotten [shakach] in the city [ir] where they had so done [asah]: this is also vapor [hebel].
10.notes: The rasha (H7563) frequented the qadosh maqom (H6918, H4725), the holy place, and got the dignified funeral the just man of 6:3 was denied. Yet shakach (H7911), the forgetting, swallows the pageant too — their memorial outlived them by a week.

11.text: Because the sentence against an evil work is not carried out swiftly, the heart of the sons of man fills up inside them with the will to do evil.
11.amp: Because sentence [pithgam — the official decree] against an evil [ra] work [maaseh] is not executed [asah] speedily [meherah], therefore the heart [leb] of the sons of men [adam] is fully set [male — filled full] in them to do evil [ra].
11.notes: pithgam (H6599) is a Persian loanword for an official decree: the warrant is signed but not served. male (H4390), filled full: delayed justice reads to the sinner as canceled justice, and the leb takes on evil like a vessel takes on water (cf. 2 Peter 3:9 for the mercy hidden in the delay).

12.text: Though a sinner does evil a hundred times and his days are drawn out, still I know this for certain: it will go well with those who fear God, who stand in reverence before His face.
12.amp: Though a sinner [chet] do evil [ra] an hundred times, and his days be prolonged [arak], yet surely I know [yada] that it shall be well [tov] with them that fear [yare] God [Elohim], which fear before [panim] Him:
12.notes: The creed spoken into the teeth of the evidence: yada (H3045), I know, set against everything verse 10 saw. The yare Elohim (H3373), the God-fearers, hold the tov (H2896) in escrow — the settlement is certain even when the court runs slow.

13.text: But it will not go well with the wicked; his days will not lengthen out like the evening shadow, because there is no fear of God before him.
13.amp: But it shall not be well [tov] with the wicked [rasha], neither shall he prolong [arak] his days [yom], which are as a shadow [tsel]; because he fears [yare] not before [panim] God [Elohim].
13.notes: tsel (H6738), the shadow again (cf. 6:12): the rasha's days may look long, but a shadow-length is borrowed light, and evening takes it back. The hinge of both verses is the same clause — before the panim of God, fearing or not fearing.

14.text: There is a vapor that is done on the earth: there are righteous men who are paid according to the deeds of the wicked, and wicked men who are paid according to the deeds of the righteous. I said, this also is vapor.
14.amp: There is [yesh] a vapor [hebel] which is done [asah] upon the earth [eretz]; that there be just [tsaddiq] men, unto whom it happens [naga — it touches, strikes] according to the work [maaseh] of the wicked [rasha]; again, there be wicked men, to whom it happens according to the work of the righteous [tsaddiq]: I said [amar] that this also [gam] is vapor [hebel].
14.notes: naga (H5060), to touch or strike: the wages land on the wrong men, paychecks swapped at the window. This is 7:15 stated as a system, the crookedness (7:13) running right through the moral ledger — observed honestly, filed under hebel, and left for the Judge of 12:14.

15.text: So I commended gladness, because under the sun a man has nothing better than to eat and to drink and to be glad, and this joy will stay beside him in his toil through the days of life God gives him under the sun.
15.amp: Then I commended [shabach] mirth [simchah], because a man [adam] has no better [tov] thing under the sun [shemesh], than to eat [akal], and to drink [shatah], and to be merry [samach]: for that shall abide with [lavah — join itself to, accompany] him of his labour [amal] the days [yom] of his life [chay], which God [Elohim] gives [natan] him under the sun.
15.notes: shabach (H7623), the commending-word he once spent on the dead (4:2), now spent on simchah (H8057). lavah (H3867) is to join and accompany: gladness as the companion that walks the whole road of the amal — the fourth sounding of the book's joy-refrain (cf. 2:24; 3:12-13; 5:18).

16.text: When I gave my heart to know wisdom and to see the business that is done on the earth — how even day and night men's eyes go without seeing sleep —
16.amp: When I applied [natan] my heart [leb] to know [yada] wisdom [chokmah], and to see [raah] the business [inyan] that is done [asah] upon the earth [eretz]: (for also there is that neither day [yom] nor night [layil] sees [raah] sleep with his eyes [ayin]:)
16.notes: inyan (H6045), the busyness-word, and the sleepless observer: the parenthesis describes the researcher himself, eyes open around the clock over the world's churning. The laborer of 5:12 sleeps sweetly; the man determined to understand everything does not.

17.text: then I saw the whole work of God, and saw this: man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun. However hard he labors to seek it, he will not find it; and even if the wise man claims to know, he cannot find it out.
17.amp: Then I beheld [raah] all the work [maaseh] of God [Elohim], that a man [adam] cannot [yakol] find out [matsa] the work that is done [asah] under the sun [shemesh]: because though a man labour [amal] to seek it out [baqash], yet he shall not find [matsa] it; yea further; though a wise [chakam] man think [amar — say, claim] to know [yada] it, yet shall he not be able [yakol] to find it.
17.notes: matsa (H4672), the finding-verb, denied three times in one verse: the chapter's last word on human comprehension. The maaseh of Elohim exceeds the maaseh under the sun that expresses it; the chakam who amar (H559), who says he knows, has only proved he stopped looking (cf. Deuteronomy 29:29; Romans 11:33).
